subject: MAP: CardioEdge POC access cadence & networking peering
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cardioedge.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <m.ruiz@cardioedge.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CardioEdge POC - next steps for access and network

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re excited to move to a short POC to validate latency and cost on a representative dataset. Before we kick off the mutual action plan, quick questions so we can align internal teams:

- Do you support a transient API key model (short-lived service account tokens) for the POC, or should we expect long-lived keys scoped to an org?
- For VPC peering, we can open a peering connection from our staging VPC (10.40.0.0/16) — any restrictions on overlapping CIDRs or required firewall ports?
- We’ll need an IP allowlist for any control-plane callbacks — is there a published list or will you provide a small set of outbound IPs?

We’re aiming to start environment provisioning next Wednesday (2028-06-07). If you can share a short MAP with owners and dates, we’ll sync with infra and network.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
CTO, CardioEdge
[Attachment: cardioedge-poc-sample-data-manifest.csv (text/csv)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cardioedge.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardioEdge POC - next steps for access and network

Alex —

Appreciate the quick follow. I’ve looped in Priyom (on access & MAP tracking) and Karthik (network/peering). Below is a concise mutual action plan we propose — short bullets with owners and dates so both infra teams have a single checklist to act from.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Org & user setup (owner: Alex / CardioEdge SRE) — create org placeholder in our onboarding portal, provide primary admin email (due: 2028-06-05)
2) API key model decision (owner: Priyom) — we support both: a) short-lived service tokens (recommended) via our ephemeral token service or b) scoped long-lived API keys (access-limited). Please confirm preference (due: 2028-06-04)
3) IP allowlist & callback IPs (owner: CardioEdge, confirm w/ Priyom) — we will publish a stable control-plane egress range; for initial POC we can also accept CIDR allowlist entries (due: 2028-06-06)
4) VPC peering window (owner: Karthik / CardioEdge network) — Karthik will propose connection window and required routing/firewall config (due: 2028-06-06)
5) Credentials & test keys (owner: Priyom) — Redwood to provision test tenant and handover keys once org created (target: 2028-06-07 provisioning)
6) Smoke test & acceptance (owner: CardioEdge & Redwood) — basic token-auth calls + sample inference runs (target acceptance: 2028-06-10)

Attachments I’m sending: Redwood MAP template (redwood-map-v1.pdf) and a short checklist you can paste into your ticketing system. We’re flexible on the API key model — short-lived tokens are preferred for security and audit.

If this looks good I’ll create a shared MAP sheet and a short 30m call Monday to lock owners.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-map-v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cardioedge.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Jun 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardioEdge POC - next steps for access and network

Alex / Evelyn —

Quick follow on the API key and peering items so your infra team can prepare:

API keys / token model:
- We recommend ephemeral service tokens for POCs to avoid key rotation overhead. Tokens are minted via our short-lived token endpoint and can be scoped to a tenant/service account.
- If you need CI-friendly long-lived keys we can create scoped API keys limited to inference-only calls (no admin APIs).

Credentials handoff process:
- Step 1: You provide admin email and desired org name -> Redwood creates tenant placeholder.
- Step 2: We create a service account and provide either: ephemeral token instructions or long-lived key material in a protected DocuSign envelope (if requested).

VPC peering / CIDR guidance (draft):
- Avoid overlapping CIDRs. Our recommended customer-side staging CIDR: 10.40.0.0/16 (you already mentioned this), we will peer from our staging range 10.80.0.0/16.
- Required outbound ports for control-plane callbacks: 443.
- For private peering we recommend adding a small static route to restrict management traffic.

I attached a fillable MAP checklist you can use to assign owners and mark readiness. Once you confirm the preferred key model I’ll queue tenant provisioning and generate the initial test keys.

[Attachment: cardioedge-map-access-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cardioedge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <m.ruiz@cardioedge.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Jun 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardioEdge POC - next steps for access and network

Thanks Priyom — that flow works. Quick specifics from our network team so you can draft the peering request: 

- Staging VPC CIDR: 10.40.0.0/16 (AWS us-west-2)
- Peering endpoints will be initiated from our side; preferred peering window: Tue 2028-06-07 02:00-04:00 UTC (we can be flexible)
- We will accept the Redwood staging CIDR 10.80.0.0/16 and will not NAT egress within the peering routes.
- Control plane callbacks will be allowed from 54.210.33.12 and 54.210.33.13 (please confirm these two are stable or whether you provide a CIDR)

We’ll take ephemeral tokens as the primary option. I’ve asked our SRE to provision an admin email and will send that in a separate note.

—Alex
Alex Turner
CTO, CardioEdge
[Quoted: "Proposed MAP (high level):" from Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com> dated Fri, 01 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: CardioEdge POC - next steps for access and network

Alex / team —

Confirming Redwood side next steps and a compact timeline for the MAP so we can close the loop:

- 2028-06-04: CardioEdge to provide admin email + desired org name (owner: Alex)
- 2028-06-05: Redwood creates tenant placeholder and shares ephemeral-token guide (owner: Priyom)
- 2028-06-06: CardioEdge to submit peering request with proposed window; include any firewall ACL entries for 54.210.33.12/13 (owner: CardioEdge)
- 2028-06-07: Redwood provisions test tenant, issues initial test tokens, and verifies peering (owner: Redwood infra / Karthik)
- 2028-06-10: Joint smoke-test and acceptance sign-off (owner: CardioEdge + Redwood)

I attached a short text file with the sample CIDR lines we use to speed firewall changes. I’ll open the peering ticket from our side once we have the admin email.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
